body.statement: Theorem 3 (fixed-input plug-in inference).  Fix one finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), fix its equality-branch circuit \(\tau\), and fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).  Every recorded denominator is positive at \(P\), so the rational circuit \(\tau\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(P\), the event defining \(\widehat\tau_n\) has probability tending to one, and \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau(P))\Rightarrow\mathcal N\left(0,J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\right)\).  Moreover, \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\).  If \(\sigma_y^2>0\), then \(\widehat\tau_{n,y}\pm1.96\sqrt{\widehat V_{n,yy}/n}\) has limiting coverage \(0.9500042097\ldots\) for \(P_x(Y=y)\).
body.justification: A certified population functional should produce standard sampling inference without graphwise duplicate estimates.
body.gap: Chang, Guo, and Malinsky handle data-driven graph selection by interval unions; this theorem instead gives pointwise plug-in inference for one fixed certified oracle, tied family, and arithmetic circuit.
body.consumer: After a population or externally certified discovery analysis, practitioners can estimate the common intervention probability with one covariance calculation.
body.proof_tex:
Fix the input, its equality-branch circuit, and \(P\) as in the proposed statement.  Since \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), every cell \(P_z\) is strictly positive.  Every recorded denominator \(B_{D,y}\) is a finite product of observed marginal probabilities.  Each such marginal is a nonempty sum of positive cells, so
\[
 B_{D,y}(P)>0\qquad\text{for every }D\in\mathfrak D\text{ and }y.
\]
There are finitely many pairs \((D,y)\).  Polynomial continuity therefore gives an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(P\) on which all these denominators remain positive.  A quotient of polynomials with nonvanishing denominator is continuously differentiable, so \(\tau\) is continuously differentiable on \(U\), with derivative \(J_\tau\).

Let \(e_z\in\mathbb R^m\) be the coordinate vector for cell \(z\), and set \(W_i=e_{Z_i}-P\).  The i.i.d. sampling assumption gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P W_i=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P(W_iW_i^{\mathsf T})
 =\operatorname{diag}(P)-PP^{\mathsf T}=\Sigma_P,
 \qquad
 \sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nW_i.
\]
For fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^m\), finite support permits a uniform third-order Taylor expansion at zero:
\[
 \mathbb E_P\exp\!\left(\frac{t^{\mathsf T}W_i}{\sqrt n}\right)
 =1+\frac{t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Pt}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}).
\]
Independence and \((1+a/n+O(n^{-3/2}))^n\to e^a\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\exp\!\left(t^{\mathsf T}\sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)\right)
 \longrightarrow \exp\!\left(\frac12t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Pt\right),
\]
the moment generating function of the possibly singular normal law \(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_P)\).  Independently, all hypotheses of the cited multivariate i.i.d. central limit theorem hold because \(W_i\) has finite support.  Therefore
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_P).
\]
Also
\[
 \mathbb E_P\|\widehat p_n-P\|_2^2=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_P)}{n}\longrightarrow0,
\]
so \(\widehat p_n\to P\) in probability.  Since \(U\) is a neighborhood of \(P\), \(\Pr_P(\widehat p_n\in U)\to1\), and in particular the denominator event in \(\mathrm{def{:}plugin\text{-}estimator}\) has probability tending to one.

Continuous differentiability gives the deterministic expansion
\[
 \tau(P+h)=\tau(P)+J_\tau(P)h+r(h),
 \qquad \frac{\|r(h)\|}{\|h\|}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The second-moment display implies \(\sqrt n\|\widehat p_n-P\|=O_P(1)\), whence \(\sqrt n\,r(\widehat p_n-P)=o_P(1)\).  This is also the remainder conclusion of the cited multivariate delta method.  The off-event definition changes the estimator only on an event of probability tending to zero.  It follows that
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_n-\tau(P)\}
 =J_\tau(P)\sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)+o_P(1)
 \Rightarrow
 \mathcal N\!\left(0,J_\tau(P)\Sigma_PJ_\tau(P)^{\mathsf T}\right).
\]

The maps \(p\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^{\mathsf T}\) and \(p\mapsto J_\tau(p)\) are continuous at \(P\).  Therefore, again ignoring an event whose probability tends to zero,
\[
 \widehat V_n
 =J_\tau(\widehat p_n)\widehat\Sigma_nJ_\tau(\widehat p_n)^{\mathsf T}
 \xrightarrow{P}J_\tau(P)\Sigma_PJ_\tau(P)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
On the equality branch, the sound certificate procedure proves that \(\tau_y(P)=T_{D,y}(P)\) for every represented causal DAG \(D\); by the truncated-factorization definition this common value is the causal cell probability \(P_x(Y=y)\), not merely an observed regression.

Finally assume the declared nondegeneracy condition \(\sigma_y^2>0\).  The scalar marginal limit, variance consistency, and the cited Slutsky lemma imply
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,y}-P_x(Y=y)\}}
 {\sqrt{\widehat V_{n,yy}}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
The boundary points \(\pm1.96\) have zero standard-normal probability, so the coverage converges to
\[
 \Pr\{-1.96\leq Z\leq1.96\}=2\Phi(1.96)-1\approx0.950004,
 \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
This proves the corrected coverage claim and every other assertion.
